requirement: Successful and failed runs preserve original fixture sources

inputs.name: default
inputs.call: check.py -> real gd-tools test --coverage with one passing and one deliberately failing test (gd-tools-cli 0.4.0 + GUT v9.7.1)

measured_with_gd_tools_0_4_0.finding: subject.gd is byte-for-byte identical on disk before and after the run, regardless of the mixed pass/fail outcome. This is a structural fact about gd-tools' instrumentation approach, not a runtime coincidence: gd-tools 0.4.0 instruments via GDScript's in-memory Script.reload(true) (confirmed by direct source reading during BP05/earlier BP06 work on the autoload fixtures), never by writing modified bytecode or source back to disk -- so there is no restoration step because there is no mutation to restore from.

notes: A clean pass, and a structurally strong one: this requirement is trivially satisfied for any tool using gd-tools' in-place-reload instrumentation strategy, since 'preserve sources' reduces to 'never touch the file', which is easy to verify and hard to violate by accident. This is a meaningfully different (and safer) approach than a hypothetical tool that instruments by rewriting source files on disk and restoring them afterward, where a crash mid-run could leave a fixture permanently mutated -- that failure mode (relevant to F066, forced termination or crash -- since built; its bound subject.gd was re-hashed unchanged after the SIGKILL run by the 2026-09-19 review pass, although F066's own check.py does not assert that) does not apply to gd-tools' architecture at all. (Stale 'currently unbuilt' wording corrected 2026-09-19 by the second-reviewer pass.)
